label: Institution
name: Kyoto University of Education
summary:
Kyoto University of Education (京都教育大学, Kyōto Kyōiku Daigaku, founded 1949 with origins in a 1876 Meiji-era normal school) is one of Japan's specialized national universities for teacher education, part of the network of prefectural and national education universities established throughout Japan to train the teachers who would staff Japan's world-class public school system — the educational infrastructure that underlay Japan's extraordinary post-Meiji economic and social development.

Japan's emphasis on teacher education as a specialized discipline reflects its national commitment to education quality: Japan developed dedicated normal schools (师範学校, shihan gakkō) from the early Meiji period (1872 education law) specifically to train professional teachers according to modern pedagogical methods. These normal schools were a cornerstone of Japan's educational modernization — ensuring that the mass public education system being created had qualified teachers trained in systematic pedagogy.

Kyoto's University of Education's location in Japan's cultural capital gives it particular significance for teacher education: Kyoto's extraordinary cultural heritage (World Heritage Sites, traditional arts, classical Japanese literature, Buddhist and Shinto traditions) makes it an exceptionally rich environment for education in Japanese cultural subjects. Teachers trained in Kyoto bring exposure to the fullest expression of Japanese traditional culture. The university contributes to the teaching profession in the Kyoto-Osaka-Kobe metropolitan area, one of Japan's most populous and culturally rich regions.
